fatal_omissions.label: Run the closing safety sweep
fatal_omissions.omission_consequence: Skip the sweep and the weapon never surfaces. The officers walk up to what they think is a quiet welfare check and it is actually a possible armed domestic.
fatal_omissions.sop_citation: Call-Taking SOP 9.4 — mandatory closing safety sweep.

step_results.label: Verify the location first
step_results.omission_consequence: If the line drops before the address is verified, there's a frightened caller and nowhere to send a unit. Location is the one thing that can't be reconstructed after the call ends.
step_results.sop_citation: Call-Taking SOP 4.2 — location before all else.

step_results.label: Open the funnel before you close it
step_results.omission_consequence: Lead with a closed or leading question and you only ever learn the one thing you thought to ask. The open question is how the overnight disturbance nobody mentioned gets found.

step_results.label: Run the closing safety sweep
step_results.omission_consequence: Skip the sweep and the weapon never surfaces. The officers walk up to what they think is a quiet welfare check and it is actually a possible armed domestic.
step_results.sop_citation: Call-Taking SOP 9.4 — mandatory closing safety sweep.

step_results.label: Re-prioritize caller safety after the upgrade
step_results.omission_consequence: Once it's a weapons call, the caller's safety is the new top of the call. Letting them wander outside or talking them out of what they heard undoes the sweep you just ran.
step_results.sop_citation: Call-Taking SOP 9.5 — caller safety after upgrade.

reflection_prompt: You just took a call that started as a welfare check and ended as a possible armed domestic. Which single question changed the whole call — and what happens to the responding officers if you skip it?
